hook: Chemotaxing amoebae use 0.25% of the molecule-uptake limit, so counting noise, not energy, limits sensing.

readout.label: Dictyostelium uptake relative to sensing limit

summary: The authors derive formulas linking gradient-sensing accuracy to the number of absorbed molecules and the entropy that absorption produces. Re-analyzing Dictyostelium chemotaxis data places the cell far below the limit with minor metabolic load. The conclusion rests on a theoretical model and on previously published data from one organism.
title: Energetic costs of reaching the physical limits of sensing
